- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.17) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤-0.22) mid-horizon, model fails to adjust downward; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per negative sentiment unit.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.00–0.17) and price is trending upward; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast if prior 3 days show upward momentum.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >+2% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 0.5–1.0% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period momentum; adjust final 5–7 days downward if sentiment is weak or negative.
